__doc: Two floors per model, as ratios (run.js --gate): `floor` for the requirements a PR does that the stage does not call a gap, `gapsFloor` for the requirements it leaves out that it calls one.

eval-fake (the wiring smoke, every PR): deterministic. The scripted judge's answer reads as a task too thin to judge, so nothing is called a gap: 42/42 done work not flagged, 0/25 gaps caught. floor = observed; a stage that judged nothing would score the same, which is why the real models carry the gaps floor.

2026-10-20, 29 cases (42 done, 25 gaps): deepseek-v4-flash@fireworks 38/43, 38/43, 37/43 done work not flagged and 23/25 in all three runs; gpt-6-sol 29/42, 30/42, 29/42 and 24/25, 22/25, 24/25. floor and gapsFloor = the lowest of the runs.

Where the false gaps come from (the runs' verdicts, read case by case): the judge reads only the diff, and the second look at the repository runs on MISSING alone, so a requirement done in a function the PR calls but does not change (validateEmail, assertRenewable, toAppointmentDto) comes back partial or check_manually; and gpt-6-sol calls a requirement partial when the diff does not show it wired end to end (a queued job that sends, a serializer the route uses).
RATCHET: a PR that moves the value on purpose (the judge, the second look, the cases) recalibrates here in the same PR, with its runs as evidence.
